name: Nichols plc
executive_summary: Nichols plc is a UK-listed, asset-light soft drinks group centred on Vimto, with diversified routes to market across UK Packaged, International Packaged and Out of Home. The quantitative screen rates the stock a buy on quality, GARP and dividend metrics (8/22 models; P/E 17.1, ROE 25.8%, yield 3.6%, PEG 0.59), though it fails classic deep-value and earnings-quality tests. Filings show a multi-year shift from volume-led revenue to margin-led profit: adjusted PBT rose from £27.2m (FY2023) to £31.4m (FY2024) and £33.6m (FY2025 per H1 2026 interim full-year comparatives), with net cash of £55.7m at end-FY2025 and £66.2m at H1 2026. The investment case rests on high adjusted ROCE, progressive dividends and international concentrate expansion; the debate is whether mid-teens adjusted PBT margins and a P/B of 4.1 already price in execution, plus CFO succession, Middle East phasing/geopolitics, and the August 2026 VITHIT acquisition (headline only in the index, no body extract).
investment_thesis: For a value investor oriented towards quality compounders rather than net-net bargains, Nichols fits the screen’s buy signal reasonably well. The name passes Lynch PEG, Neff PEGY, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula and Financial Health—consistent with a franchise business generating adjusted ROCE above 27% (31.0% FY2024; 30.4% H1 2025; 27.9% H1 2026) on minimal capital intensity. Revenue growth looks modest in reported terms (£172.8m → £175.1m FY2024–FY2025) because management is deliberately migrating African markets from finished-goods to higher-margin concentrate sales, which suppresses top line but expands gross margin (45.7% FY2024; resilient ~44% at interim). UK Packaged continues to compound through innovation (Wonderfuel, Vimto Energy, Myprotein partnership) and distribution gains; OoH has been restructured for profit after exiting unprofitable accounts and Starslush. Balance-sheet optionality—net cash throughout, no external bank borrowings at each going-concern confirmation—supports the progressive dividend policy (cover moving from ~2.0x to 1.5x adjusted earnings in 2026) and selective M&A. The screen’s failures (Graham, Schloss, FCF yield, Piotroski 6/9, OCF below earnings) correctly flag that this is not statistically cheap on book or cash-yield grounds; the buy case is GARP-on-quality, not deep value.
financial_review:
Primary source: UK RNS filing bodies under `filings/bodies/`. FY2025 full preliminary results (11 March 2026) and the VITHIT acquisition RNS (10 August 2026) are indexed but lack downloadable body extracts; FY2025 annual figures below are taken from audited comparatives embedded in the H1 2026 interim filing and the 14 January 2026 FY25 Trading Update.

Annual trend (FY2023–FY2025)

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Revenue | £170.7m | £172.8m | £175.1m |
| Adjusted PBT | £27.2m | £31.4m | £33.6m |
| Adjusted PBT margin | 15.9% | 18.2% | ~19.2% |
| Adjusted EPS (basic) | 56.41p | 64.02p | 67.53p |
| Statutory PBT | £24.3m | £24.0m | £29.2m |

| Adjusted ROCE | 26.3% | 31.0% | n/a in extract |
| Net cash | £67.0m | £53.7m | £55.7m |
| FCF (pre-dividend definition) | £20.9m | £17.8m | n/a in annual body |

FY2024 (2024 Preliminary Results, 11 March 2025): Revenue +1.2% to £172.8m; adjusted operating profit +14.6% to £28.9m; adjusted PBT +15.6% to £31.4m (margin 18.2%); adjusted EPS 64.02p (+13.5%). Statutory operating profit fell 3.6% to £21.5m after £7.4m exceptional ERP costs. FCF £17.8m; net cash £53.7m after £31.2m dividends including a £20.0m special (54.8p). Total ordinary dividend proposed 32.0p (+13.4%). Cash conversion 76% (vs 102% prior year), partly reflecting cash-funded exceptionals. Defined-benefit pension surplus £3.7m.

FY2025 (trading update 14 January 2026; audited figures from H1 2026 interim comparatives): Revenue +1.3% to £175.0m; Africa like-for-like +10%; UK Packaged +2.6%; cash £55.8m year-end. Full-year adjusted PBT £33.6m and adjusted EPS 67.53p per H1 2026 interim audited column; statutory PBT £29.2m after £4.4m ERP-related exceptionals (programme completed March 2025). Proposed final dividend 18.7p per 23 March 2026 annual report publication notice (body lacks full accounts).

Interim progression

H1 2025 (31 July 2025): Revenue +1.8% to £85.5m; adjusted PBT +0.8% to £14.6m; adjusted EPS 29.90p; net cash £61.6m; FCF £14.2m. Exceptionals £3.2m (ERP). FY25 adjusted PBT expected in line with consensus £33.1m.

H1 2026 (29 July 2026): Revenue +4.7% to £89.5m; adjusted PBT +2.7% to £15.0m; adjusted EPS 30.30p; statutory PBT £15.0m with zero exceptionals (vs £3.2m prior year); net cash £66.2m; record H1 operating cash flow £21.9m; FCF £17.3m. Interim dividend raised 34.7% to 20.2p under revised 1.5x cover policy. FY26 consensus adjusted PBT £35.1m; full-year guidance maintained.

Trading updates corroborate momentum: Q1 2026 revenue +4.3% to £41.0m (21 April 2026 AGM update); international growth weighted to H2 due to Ramadan/concentrate shipment phasing—management flagged H1 FY26 profitability could be modestly below prior year while full-year expectations unchanged.

Cash flow and screen reconciliation: Filings define FCF as net cash increase before acquisitions and dividends. Yahoo (`financials_annual.json`, fallback) shows operating cash flow £13.8m and FCF £12.7m for FY2025—below filing-reported £17.8m (FY2024) and H1 2026 FCF £17.3m, and the screen flags OCF below net income (Piotroski). Working-capital swings (receivables +£8.2m FY2025 per Yahoo) warrant monitoring; H1 2026 notes full reversal of year-end outflows.

Gaps: No body extract for FY2025 Preliminary Results (March 2026) or VITHIT acquisition terms; 2025 and 2026 annual report publication notices contain dividend timetables only, not full financial statements. FY2023 annual report not in body set—FY2023 comparatives cited from FY2024 preliminary filing.
risks_and_flags:
Regulatory and category: Filings cite evolving soft-drink regulation, UK Deposit Return Scheme implementation, and climate/ESG-driven legislation as principal risks (H1 2026 interim, cross-referencing 2025 annual report pages 63–69). Health-and-wellness trends require continuous portfolio refresh.

Geopolitical and phasing: Middle East conflict and Yemen/Ukraine supply-chain sensitivities appear in going-concern and trading-update language; Ramadan timing creates volatile H1/H2 revenue mix (Middle East H1 2025 revenue £1.6m vs £3.5m prior year). Africa concentrate transition improves margins but obscures reported growth.

Governance and key person: CFO Richard Newman’s passing (March 2025 RNS, no body) disrupted finance leadership; Matthew Rothwell appointed CFO April 2026 after interim roles (David Taylor, Rebecca Hughes). Non-executive succession (Alan Williams replacing John Gittins) proceeded smoothly, but family representation on the board (John and Matthew Nichols) remains. AGM poll showed ~9.5% opposition to chair re-election (April 2025).

Operational: ERP go-live (March 2025) consumed £7.6m cumulative exceptionals; benefits realisation now key. Historic HMRC incentive scheme (£4.3m settlement 2022) with ongoing employee debt recovery—provision unchanged at H1 2025.

Competitive: International Middle East faces increased category competition despite Vimto’s Iftar dominance; UK squash is number two, not leader.

M&A: Acquisition of VITHIT announced 10 August 2026 (index only; no terms, financing or synergy disclosure in available bodies)—integration and capital allocation risk ahead of verify-before-trade.

Accounting/quality: Screen fails Earnings Quality and Piotroski (OCF < earnings, leverage not declining, asset turnover flat). Not a going-concern issue—directors affirm adequate resources with net cash and no external borrowings at each review—but cash conversion merits scrutiny.

Pension: UK defined-benefit scheme in surplus (£3.7–3.9m); actuarial remeasurements create OCI volatility, not a funding deficit.

news_highlights:
News coverage in `news_manifest.json` is thin: a single Yahoo Finance article, “The Trend Of High Returns At Nichols (LON:NICL) Has Us Very Interested” (12 February 2026), highlighting return on capital—not substantive new information.

Material developments over the past year come primarily from RNS headlines in the filings index rather than press coverage:

- Strategy: Capital Markets Day (November 2024) medium-term target of ~20% PBT margin; ongoing Africa concentrate migration; Wonderfuel functional squash (March 2025); Myprotein Clear Whey Protein Water with THG (July/August 2026).
- Management: CFO succession after Richard Newman’s death; Matthew Rothwell appointed CFO (April 2026); Alan Williams joined board (March 2025); John Gittins retired (August 2025).
- Corporate: FY2024 special dividend 54.8p (£20m); dividend cover policy revised to 1.5x (March 2026); proposed acquisition of VITHIT (10 August 2026)—details not in body extracts.
- Trading: FY25 and Q1 FY26 updates in line with consensus; Middle East conflict monitoring with mitigation plans (April 2026 AGM update).
research_rationale: Primary filings confirm a cash-rich, high-ROCE quality compounder with accelerating H1 2026 trends and a dividend-supported total-return profile, broadly supporting the quantitative buy signal, while valuation, earnings-quality screen failures, CFO transition and thin disclosure on the VITHIT deal prevent full conviction.
